notes: Web 423 — TIMER-PAUSED-ITSELF-NOV11 (Nov 11, 2026). The owner's 16:33 CST report, with his screen recording: 'I just opened the app to see the count. And found it paused.. Without any action from me! Now it's off by 1.5 hours!' The card read Paused with 07:59:57 banked from the 8:00 AM start — a full day's counting folded at ~16:00 by no tap of his. He had fully closed and reopened the app at ~14:39 to load webs 421/422 and the session resumed; the pause landed after that. His law since Nov 7: a running timer pauses ONLY on his tap or a day close. Web 365 closed the two stamp-arbitrated roads (the cloudsync v361 rule, the adoption flip) — both engage only when the copies carry deliberate-transition stamps that DIFFER. The full inventory of pause writers on web 422 bytes (js/app.js, js/cloudsync.js, js/shifttrack.js, js/splitshift.js, native SessionRecord.java) leaves two roads that land a PAUSED state on a running session with no tap on his device, both proven in bench on 422 bytes (tools/timer-autopause-v423-test.js). ROAD 1 — THE CLOUD STAMP GAME: copies of the SAME session restored on another of his surfaces carry the session's stateAt VERBATIM (restores and ordinary saves never re-stamp it; only transitions do), so a paused copy of this session — folded on another surface, or left by an echo — reaches the pull with an EQUAL stamp; the v361 rule never engages and the generic game installs the copy wholesale (a settled local key takes it unconditionally; a both-changed key takes it on the doc stamp alone); js/app.js onAuth then re-reads the store copy into the live page and the running timer stands paused mid-flight. A stateAt-less paused copy (a legacy shell) takes the same road — the rule needs both stamps > 0. ROAD 2 — THE REOPEN RESTORE: adoptSessionRecord's idle-page restore adopted a PAUSED record on its SAVE stamp alone (stateNewer — and a relaunched page's _lastStateAt resets to 0, so the contest is no contest), so any paused record a reopen met became the page's truth wholesale, bank and all — his exact 07:59:57 card. THE FIX (two guards, nothing else touched): (1) js/cloudsync.js — a cloud copy may NEVER install a PAUSED state over a locally RUNNING copy of the same session (pins within the v361 jitter family, or a pin-less copy), whatever stamps it carries: the local stands and the key stays dirty (the tombstone idiom) so the flush pushes the running truth UP. Untouched: a local pause (a later deliberate resume still installs over it), the v411 close (installs IDLE, never a pause), the v265 later-session rule and different-session arbitration. (2) js/app.js — the reopen restore adopts a record's PAUSED state only when the record carries a deliberate-transition stamp (stateAt > 0: every real pause writer stamps one — his page tap, his face tap, a web-surface tap, the split engine); an UNSTAMPED paused record is no one's tap, so the session restores RUNNING with its banked time preserved whole and its segment re-anchored at the restore moment — no counted time lost, no phantom pause landed. His own face-tap pause (stamped, src 'native') still restores exactly as paused, the v365 face-tap flip of a running page is byte-untouched, and the split engine's deliberate self-pause (split-day accounts only) stands. Bench: the new suite 27/27 on the fixed tree; on pristine web 422 bytes the same suite passes 18/27, failing exactly today's shapes (settled pull installs the pause; both-changed pull installs it — the bench log even prints 'conflict on tracker -> cloud won'; stateAt-less copy installs it; the reopen adopts the unstamped pause at his exact 07:59:57 bank). One standing assertion updated with a supersession note: morning-leg-v361 S5 expected a stateAt-less local to fall through to the old stamp game — that fall-through IS Road 1, and its expectation is now the v423 law (the running session stands); the scenario is unchanged. Regression vs pristine 422, identical standings: close-shuts-timer-v411 36/36, counting-phantom-taps-nov11 15/15, counting-repeg-fail-nov11 16/16, phantom-root-nov11 44/44, web412-three-fixes 43/43, sync-flap-v413 7/7, session-relaunch-v93 and v94 fail identically on both (native-source pins against the sibling repo, pre-existing); timer-stopped-by-itself-v365 and morning-leg-v361 carry only their stale version-pin failures once this release's manifest lands. Verdict owed in his hands: the timer must now run until HE pauses or stops it or the day is closed — through syncs, foreground returns, full closes and reopens. Today's lost stretch (~1.5 h by his count) is not recoverable by the app; at close-out his own figures govern the ticket, as always. | Web 422 — COUNTING-PHANTOM-TAPS-NOV11 (Nov 11, 2026). The second counting defect of the day, from the owner's 13:55 screen recording: the card read 'Loads today: 8 — 2 counted from your pegs · +6 your taps'. His words: 'There were four loads until I tipped last time. Now it's making up four extra loads I don't even know where it got that from. Eight.' Timeline: 13:27 the card showed correction +1; he tapped +1 once for the missed post-re-peg tip (+2, total 4); by 13:55 the taps read +6 with NO further tap — phantom taps minted in exact multiples of his real correction. Root, proven in bench on web 421 bytes (tools/counting-phantom-taps-nov11-test.js — the real js/app.js tracker regions, v314 slice pattern, plus the real js/geoloads.js): the native session record carries the day's correction as a STANDING TOTAL (rec.loadsCorr, written by the record's keeper and zeroed only when a web consume-sync APPLIES), but adoptSessionRecord's loads branch fed that total whole to GeoLoads.nudge — a DELTA api (corrNow += delta) — on every adoption whose stamp won. The stamp is weak: App._lastLoadsAt is stamped only by this layer's own hero taps, never by an adoption, and it resets to 0 on every relaunch, while the record's updatedAt re-stamps on native writes and collects keep arriving (foreground collects, sessionRecord reads, applied === false echoes). Whenever the consume-sync was refused (the revision lost to another client), hung (App._sessSyncing stuck — the v94 shape), or never landed (the page died first), the keeper never zeroed its copy and the SAME record re-entered adoption and minted the day's whole correction again: bench corr runs 2 → 4 → 6 → 8 across three collects of one record — his afternoon digit for digit. THE FIX (js/app.js, the loads branch only — the only record-driven nudge caller; the hero taps keep their true ±1 deltas): consumption is the EXCESS — nudge only what the record claims beyond the correction this layer already holds (GeoLoads.today().corr), never less, so a standing record can neither re-mint nor un-mint a tap however often it is collected, and the consumed stamp is banked into App._lastLoadsAt so the same record cannot re-fire inside the lifetime either. A record that genuinely moves ahead (a correction made on another surface) still crosses — exactly the excess, exactly once. Bench: the new suite 15/15 (two real taps + repeated collects / refused consume-syncs / a full relaunch all hold corr at exactly +2 forever; an unseen +1 crosses once; a record at +3 over a held +2 lands exactly +3 once; a stale record claiming +1 against a held +2 changes nothing). On pristine 421 bytes the same suite passes only 5/15. Regression: every suite that exercises the shipped adoption code is unchanged — close-shuts-timer-v411 36/36, web412-three-fixes 43/43, sync-flap-v413 7/7, phantom-revival-v303 24/24, and close-end-future-v270 (58/1), edit-start-durability-v265 (23/5), phantom-converge-v271 (16/3), phantom-session-v314 (19/1) fail identically on pristine 421 (pre-existing); the counting family is untouched and at its web 421 standings (counting-repeg-fail-nov11 16/16, v416 26/26, v284 34/34, geofence 58/58, all others as recorded for 421). Ships together with web 421's GPS-miss fix (the peg-frame/face-adoption/carry fix), which remains required and unchanged. Verdict owed in his hands: taps he makes must stay exactly the taps he made, through syncs, collects and relaunches. | Web 421 — COUNTING-REPEG-FAIL-NOV11 (Nov 11, 2026). The owner's live counting test FAILED on web 420: loads 1-2 counted from his pegs in the morning; at 12:28 PM he re-pegged the pickup at a new site (the day's count held — the 416 banking works); the load he then hauled and TIPPED did not count by itself, and freshening the dump peg at the dump at 12:49 PM did not save it either — he hand-tapped it (card: 'Loads today: 3 — 2 counted from your pegs, +1 your tap'). Root, proven by instrumented bench replay of the day (tools/counting-repeg-fail-nov11-test.js, failing-first on 420 bytes): TWO defects in the peg counter (js/geoloads.js, the only file changed). (1) THE SITE FRAME WAS A FENCE: the counter frames the day as a circle on the pair's midpoint ending ~100 m past each seed (the v409 widening measured a learned scale from the midpoint and fed priors to the visit counter only), so a tip face past the dump peg — the normal case on a working fill site, where the face advances past the morning's peg — fell outside the frame, and the wrapper discarded EVERY fix there as 'off-site' before the zone machine could see the visit: no dwell built, no shadow clock ran, no recovery cluster formed (offset probe on 420 bytes: a face at the peg or +100 m counts; +150 m and beyond never counts at the tip, and a shadow candidate born on the drive-in froze mid-clock and could confirm late on a later pass). His law: pegs are SEEDS NOT FENCES. (2) THE FRESHEN ATE THE CARRY: the 12:49 dump re-peg, tapped at the dump mid-visit, rebuilt the counter with the v392 seed 'at-dump, unarmed' — the carry the outgoing machine had already proven at the pickup was discarded with the rebuild, so that visit became baseline too. THE FIX: (a) the peg counter's frame now reaches past the seeds by the dump site's own EFFECTIVE scale — the v409 profile's land-use prior or learned scale, whichever runs further, passed by the glue as cfg.profileScaleM — and the recovery cluster may build anywhere within that scale; a cluster that holds a full declared-place dwell BEYOND the 200 m recovery band ADOPTS its face in one step (the v409 proveFace chain: a proven face teaches the site's reach immediately), after which the ordinary fence/shadow discipline confirms the arrival from the adopted centre — adoption itself counts nothing. Adoption is gated twice: the face must belong DECISIVELY to the waiting end (nearer that centre than the other by 100 m+, so the v284 off-axis washroom stop, equidistant from both ends, adopts and drags nothing) and the truck must be at the cluster on its latest RAW fix (the cluster is built from smoothed fixes, and after a long drive the smoothed position trails the truck for minutes — a cluster can mature on that ghost while the truck sits on the true peg; the v416 S6 park caught exactly this in regression and the gate is what restored it). Counters built with no profile keep the v284 frame and band byte-for-byte, and the in-band 25 m nudge walk is untouched. (b) A rebuild that finds the outgoing cycle counter ARMED and the truck standing at the (re-)pegged dump is born still carrying (zone 'out', phase 'to-dump', armed) instead of 'at-dump, unarmed': the visit in progress must still prove itself by dwell, but a re-peg can no longer eat a proven carry; a declaration with no proven carry behind it keeps the v392/v369 baseline exactly. Bench: the new suite 16/16 (morning exactly 2 from the pegs; re-peg preserves the count; tips AT the peg count; tips at a face 400 m past the peg count on the FIRST post-re-peg cycle; the mid-visit freshen cycle counts; a moved face on an untouched day counts; guards: an armed pass by the face, a 5-minute armed stop 5 km off the corridor, lingering after a tip, and an unarmed 5 minutes at the face all count nothing). On pristine 420 bytes the same suite passes only 8/16 (the control and the guards), failing exactly the day's shape. Regression vs the pristine-420 baseline: every previously-green counting suite stays green — v416 dispatch-seed 26/26, v267 19/19, v268 16/16, learning 32/32, v300 recovery 14/14, v140 38/38, nov9 re-peg 15/15, v393 round-2 13/13, nov10 re-peg 22/22, v282 26/26, v283 22/22, v284 seeds-not-fences 34/34, geofence 58/58, v405 dispatch-pin 26/26, v409 dynamic-learning 30/30, dynamic-routing 10/10, role-swap 9/9, phantom-root 44/44, phantom-day 27/27, v411 close-timer 36/36, v415 dispatch-links 41/41 — and the pre-existing stale suites fail identically on both (v324 1/36, v369 0/23, jargon 33/35, v323 7/20, monday-v300 39/40). Verdict owed in his hands: the next re-pegged day must count its first post-re-peg tip by itself. | Web 420 — MERGED MANIFEST (Nov 11, 2026). Two ships landed minutes apart under the number 419 — NAV-ML-LEARNING stage 1 (js/navlearn.js + index.html wiring) and PHANTOM-ROOT-NOV11 (js/app.js booking gate + modules/invoice.js entry-level vouch) — and the second ship's version.json, built on the 418 tree, replaced the first's, leaving the files manifest stale for index.html and missing js/navlearn.js. No code from either ship was lost (the pushes touch disjoint files; verified blob-by-blob against both remote commits). This release changes NO app code: version.json is rebuilt from the true merged tree so the manifest matches every live file, and the number moves to 420 so every client converges. | Web 419 — PHANTOM-ROOT-NOV11 (Nov 11, 2026). Web 418's invoice-side fix did NOT kill the Sunday Nov 1 phantom in the owner's hands: the entry survived (he deleted it by hand) and he testified he neither started a session that Sunday nor had auto-start set for it. Root, proven in code: stopSessionAt — the ONLY writer of session records — booked whatever the tracker claimed at stop time (date from the stop day, seconds from the tracker's current claim) with no check that a start ever occurred on the day being booked and no agreement check against the session's pin, which is what every guard (stale heal, closed-day proof, adoption) judges by; the heals reach a shell only on the dashboard tick / visibility cadence, so a stop landing first minted the phantom (the Oct 25 shell booked $136.21 exactly this way). And 418's builder vouched a whole DAY from any one genuinely-started record while Revenue's onSession replaces the day's tracker entry at every stop, so a shell stopping later became the day's entry behind a small genuine record's vouch. Fix, at the two choke points: (1) stopSessionAt's booking gate — judged by the pin first, a cross-day session books only as a genuine overnight carry (pin and derived start naming the same day, the day right before the stop day, span under 24 h, start day not already closed) and then books onto its ORIGINAL start day, never re-dated; any other cross-day stop buries the session exactly like the stale heal (engines and native stood down, tracker idle with the discard marker) and writes NO session entry, NO cloud doc and NO Revenue line; any failure inside the gate falls through to the old behaviour. (2) The shared builder: a tracker entry whose own session hours match a shell record's hours for its date and no genuine record's hours is the shell's booking and never becomes a line; an entry matching neither (a Day Details edit) is untouched. Bench: tools/phantom-root-nov11-test.js 44/44 (the Nov 1 shape — Oct 31 pin, 14.78h banked, stopped Nov 1 — writes nothing; a genuine 22:00 to 01:00 carry books on Oct 31; the mixed-day builder case that reproduced the exact $428.71 line on 418 bytes now emits no line); the suite fails 24 assertions on pristine web 418 bytes. 418's phantom-day suite 39/39 and every stop/invoice neighbour suite unchanged (the six stale version-pin suites fail identically on 418 and 419). | Web 418 — PHANTOM-DAY-NOV1 / GHOST-AUTO-NOV8 / NOV2-SAVE-BLOCK (Nov 11, 2026). Owner screenshot, invoice Line items for Nov 1–15: a 14.78h / $428.71 'from tracker — unconfirmed' line for Nov 1 (a Sunday, his day off — he never worked it), a $0.01 'Auto from tracker' line for Nov 8 (also a Sunday day off), and a red banner refusing to save the invoice at all because Nov 2 holds more than one tracker entry with no dispatch completion. Investigation: every 'Auto from tracker' entry is written by Revenue.onSession from the ONE stopSessionAt path in js/app.js, which dates the session record by its END day — so a session started Oct 31 and only stopped on Nov 1 books its whole span onto Nov 1; the v303/v314 stale-session heals discard such cross-day shells only at cold open / sign-in / first pull, so a stop that lands first books the shell. The $0.01 is a ~1-second session: onSession stores hours rounded to '0.00' but prices from the UNROUNDED hours, so a drip becomes a cent. The save block is invIssue's v79 duplicate refusal. Fixes, all inside the ONE shared day-builder (invCycBuildRevenueLines, consumed by Revenue, the invoice, P&L, the manifest and the dispatch day-earnings read, so they can never disagree): (1) PHANTOM-DAY-NOV1 — the builder takes the sessions store as an optional 6th argument (every first-party caller now passes it): a tracker-sourced day surfaces only if some session record genuinely STARTED that day — its own start (endedAt − seconds, the derivation Revenue's day detail itself uses) falls on the record's own date. Cross-midnight shells and days with no session record produce no line and no duplicate flag. With no sessions evidence the builder behaves exactly as before. (2) GHOST-AUTO-NOV8 — a tracker entry under 0.1 of the pay standard's unit never becomes a line, unconditionally: the same never-money rule Revenue's entryMoneyFlags has held since v116, now spoken by the builder too. (3) NOV2-SAVE-BLOCK — invIssue no longer refuses on duplicateDates; the builder already leaves an unresolved duplicate day OFF the invoice's lines, which is exactly Revenue's own totals rule, and the editor's red '⛔ Saving is blocked' banner is now a plain amber note naming the excluded day. Dispatch and manual entries are never touched, and nothing in his real days moves: Nov 4 11h/$319.00, Nov 5 10h/$290.00, Nov 7 10.5h/$304.50, Nov 9 12.5h/$362.50, Nov 10 7.5h/$217.50 price byte-identical. The phantom ENTRIES themselves still sit in his Revenue records (the builder decides what surfaces; it does not rewrite his books) — deleting the Nov 1 / Nov 8 records in Revenue remains his tap if he wants them gone, and Nov 2's two tracker entries still need his Revenue fix to ever count, but they no longer block invoicing. The v79 duplicate assertions in tools/invoice-cycle-test.js are updated with a supersession note. Bench: tools/phantom-day-nov11-test.js 27/27 — the exact Nov 1 cross-midnight shape, the no-record shape, the no-evidence fallback, the Nov 8 drip (with/without evidence, genuine session or not), a genuine tracker-only day still lining unconfirmed, Nov 2 duplicate excluded yet invIssue succeeding and archiving, the five real days unchanged, and the full screenshot period totalling exactly $1,493.50 over five lines. Neighbours green: invoice-cycle 169/169, revenue-grouped 32/32, invoice-format 78/78, invoice-billto-notes-v298 40/40, revenue-dup-entry-v241 14/14, revenue-paycycle-v302 54/54, revenue-detail-strip-nov10 16/16. (revenue-autoprice-v152, manifest-multiday-summary-v331 and manifest-hours-source-v345 each carry the same 2 stale version-pin failures on pristine 417 — pre-existing, untouched.) Verdict owed in his hands: the Nov 1–15 invoice must show only his five real days, carry the amber Nov 2 note instead of the red block, and save.
